pr_title: Honor PropertyNamingPolicy, PropertyNameCaseInsensitive, & Encoder options when (de)serializing KeyValuePair instances
pr_body:
- Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1197

    This is a breaking change in that we'll potentially serialize the property names differently than in .NET Core 3.x/System.Text.Json 4.7.x (as influenced by the naming policy & encoder). However, roundtripping is not broken as the literals "Key" and "Value" are special-cased to match when deserializing, to accommodate payloads that were serialized with previous versions.

- Pushes code coverage for KeyValuePair converter to 100% (previously 70% line, 77% branch)

Is the JSON Path correct in these cases?

We don't create `JsonPropertyInfo` instances for the key and value properties, so JSON path will not point directly to them, but to the property name for the KVP instance.

I think this granularity is good enough, but I'll estimate the effort to get the specific path then create an issue.

Keep in mind that there is already an issue for general consistency of JSON Path https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/31955, but sounds like you want to do something scoping only KVP, so maybe make sure to link them.

We can cache these on this class as above (and don't have to pair to the options class) only because this type is internal and a new instance is created for every options instance. If this was public and\or we expected different option instances to be passed to read\write then we'd have to pair it to the options instance.

Yes, I have an iteration that caches them on the options instance, but this way is bit cleaner for now (at the cost of doing the conversions for every KeyValuePair<,> type in the object graph, rather than once (lazily) for each options instance).

Why the value should be affected by the policy?
Oh nvm, `Value` is a property on `KeyValuePair`.

So this would break someone if all of these conditions are true:
- Case insensitivity off
- Previously serialized JSON (from a previous release) is deserialized with "Key" and "Value"
- There is a naming policy such as camel-casing that changes "Key"\"Value" to something else.

That was what we last discussed (offline). However, by adding specific checks for ["Key"](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/36424/files#diff-17f25b109d239741ebe3cc5c877d272dR151) and ["Value"](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/36424/files#diff-17f25b109d239741ebe3cc5c877d272dR158), we end up not breaking any one wrt. deserialization.
I see. I missed the check for explicit clr name.
Did you consider using `ThrowInvalidOperationException_SerializerPropertyNameNull`?
I did. It's achievable with some refactoring. We don't create a `JsonPropertyInfo` for the "Key" and "Value" properties, so we'd have to pass the property names by hand.

We compare against `KeyNameCLR` and `ValueNameCLR` just to make this less of a breaking change, right? And hence, we should not honor `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive` similar to `_keyName` in this case, is that correct?

Yes. `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive` applies to matching against the result of the conversion by the naming policy. We previously serialized only "Key" & "Value", so we only care about those two literals.
